heroHeadline: North Korea Fires 12th Weapons Test of 2026 as US-South Korea Cut Joint Drill Short
heroSubtitle: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff detected roughly 10 short-range ballistic missiles fired from the greater Pyongyang area toward the East Sea on August 20, 2026 — DPRK's 12th weapons test of the year — two days after Kim Yo-jong dismissed Trump's decision to 'substantially reduce' the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise as changing nothing about the drills' 'provocative, aggressive nature.' The US and South Korean militaries formally wrapped up the shortened drill on August 21, six days ahead of schedule, having skipped its counteroffensive-focused second phase and cancelled roughly half of the planned joint field exercises. Trump has separately said he expects to meet Kim later this year and, for the first time, cited a specific nuclear arsenal figure — '57 very powerful nuclear weapons' — above SIPRI's ~50 estimate and South Korea's own 80–120 range.
footerNote: Data sourced from US/ROK official reports, KCNA, UN panels, IAEA, and institutional analyses. North Korea does not publish national statistics — economic figures are estimates with wide uncertainty ranges.
